summary: The note surveys sky quakes, unexplained booms from the sky reported worldwide and increasing since September 2023. It sets folklore explanations (Jormungandr, the Thunderbird, the Aztec Sixth Sun) beside scientific efforts, from USGS investigators to interdisciplinary studies, across incidents in Norway, Iowa, Mexico, Scotland, Prague, North Carolina and Chile. It argues that science and oral tradition both help people make sense of the phenomenon.
one_line: Sky quakes, unexplained booms from the sky reported worldwide since September 2023, are examined through folklore, scientific theories, and local case studies.
key_facts: Sky quakes are sudden, seismic booms that come from the sky without warning and have been recorded across the globe; incidents have escalated since September 2023.
On 15 September 2023, villagers of Hjallerup in Norway were startled by a sonic disruption, and elders linked it to Jormungandr, the Midgard Serpent, heralding Ragnarok.
In North American Native American heritage, the Thunderbird's wings were said to make the heavens roar.
After an event in Cedar Rapids, Iowa, on the early morning of November 2, 2023, Dr. Lillian Reeves, a geophysicist with the U.S. Geological Survey, led a team investigating the cause.
Reeves's team leaned toward undisclosed aircraft sonic booms as the cause but had no concrete evidence, since military cooperation and transparency were minimal.
In Durango, Mexico, a sequence of sky quakes persisted throughout December 2023, with the first on December 6th; the skies stayed clear.
José Aguilar, a Durango historian, compared the quakes to the Aztec legend of the Sixth Sun.
Scientific explanations include sudden releases of underground gases and shifting tectonic plates beneath the ocean, but not all incidents fit them.
Repeated sky quakes in Appin, Scotland, in January 2024 defied conventional wisdom; local weatherman Ian MacGregor suggested a link to unusual wind patterns.
In February 2024, Professors Amy Chen and Rodrigo Vargas of the University of Buenos Aires began a joint project blending atmospheric science with cultural anthropology.
On March 15, 2024, sounds from the sky over Prague reminded Petra Novak of her grandmother's stories of vengeful spirits in the sky.
Chapel Hill, North Carolina, held community gatherings in April 2024 where old legends were shared beside scientific conjecture.
Maria Garcia of the Chilean National Seismological Center tracked an unusual series of sky quakes in Santiago in May 2024.
